subject: Proposal: limited concession for uptime variance (Novus Retail)
messages:
From: Liam Harper <liam@novusretail.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.example.com
Cc: contracts@novusretail.com
Date: 2026-11-03T15:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Availability blip on 10/29 - request for remediation

Markus —

Thanks for the quick post-mortem. We saw a ~12 minute window of higher error rates during our peak processing window (10/29 13:05–13:17 UTC) which pushed a subset of traffic to fallback endpoints. The immediate business impact was order confirmation delays and a small re-send of notifications.

Novus has a 99.95% monthly uptime SLO in our MSA; we understand variability happens, but at our scale this event pushed us below the monthly target. We need to discuss a remediation path — specifically we want to understand credits or a short-term service allowance while you finalize the runtime mitigations.

What can Redwood offer? We prefer a simple bill credit or a free month applied to Novus for November (we're heavy usage in Q4). If you prefer a different structure, please propose it and include the ledger impact.

-Liam
Head of Platform Operations
Novus Retail

[Attachment: ops-timeline-novus-1029.pdf]

From: markus_klein@redwood.example.com
To: Liam Harper <liam@novusretail.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: 2026-11-04T08:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Availability blip on 10/29 - request for remediation

Liam — thanks for the note and the timeline. We recognise the impact and I want to be pragmatic here.

Quick summary of what we've done so far:
- Root cause: a partial autoscaler mis-evaluated a transient kernel stall during a GC-heavy batch, which slightly increased queuing latency for one placement group.
- Mitigations deployed: kernel selection fallback + tighter load shedding policy rolled globally (rolled 11/02).
- Ongoing: infra team is validating extended soak tests; we expect final patch by 11/12.

Proposed concession (first pass):
- Option A (simple): one month of service credit applied to Novus' November invoice equivalent to 15% of November usage (estimated $45k).
- Option B (targeted): prorated credit covering the impacted hour plus a goodwill voucher (equivalent value, $45k) redeemable across next 3 billing cycles.

I'd like to align internally on the exact ask and get exec signoff before returning an official offer. Jordan / Marissa — can you review the numbers and advise if this fits standard precedent? I'll include Karthik for any SLA/legal constraints.

Thanks,
Markus
VP, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: SLO-incident-timeline-Novus-20261103.pdf]

From: jordan_blake@redwood.example.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
Date: 2026-11-05T11:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Availability blip on 10/29 - request for remediation

Markus — quick calc notes:
- November estimated usage (current forecast): $300k
- 15% credit ~= $45k (Option A) — this mirrors recent one-off credits we gave for similar partial-impact incidents.
- Option B is operationally equivalent from a dollar perspective but gives Novus a voucher to use over time, which they asked for.

Operational risk: we should avoid setting a template larger than 25% for partial-window outages. For anything above that we need exec legal signoff and a product remediation timeline.

My recommended path to speed resolution: propose Option B (voucher + incident hour prorate) and include a 60-day validity on the voucher to encourage near-term usage. That preserves the commercial relationship and limits downstream budget erosion.

Marissa — can you route this up to the exec approvals queue? If legal needs language, Karthik can add the MSA clause references.

-Jordan
Director, Account Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

> On 2026-11-04, at 08:22, markus_klein@redwood.example.com wrote:
> Markus — thanks for the note and the timeline...

From: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.example.com, jordan_blake@redwood.example.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
Date: 2026-11-07T20:18:00Z
Subject: Exec approval: concession path for Novus (DEAL-4982)

Team —

I reviewed Jordan's calc and the precedent set in prior partial-impact incidents. Legal confirms MSA allows remedial credits for SLO misses; accounting has logged the potential $45k impact. Per the commercial playbook and given Novus' strategic Q4 volume, I approve the following offer to send to the customer:

Final offer to Novus Retail (approved):
- Concession structure: voucher equal to 15% of November forecasted usage (estimated $45,000) applied as a credit.
- Voucher specifics: redeemable across up to three billing cycles, must be used within 60 days of issue.
- Operational makegood: expedited access to our priority mitigation queue and a joint incident review call (week of 11/15).

Please have Sales Ops generate the credit memo and Contracts prepare a short amendment (1 paragraph) referencing the MSA SLO remediation clause. Markus — you can send this offer to Liam with the timeline and attached worksheet.

Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Operations (acting)
Redwood Inference
